section: Prediction and Efect Verification of Thiamine as a Leveling Agent in Chip Wafer Electroplating
text: ABSTRACT: Thiamine, a nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compound, is explored for the first time as a novel leveling agent in this study. Based on the density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the adsorption process of thiamine and the commonly used leveling agent JGB, the average values of the binding energies after equilibrium of thiamine and JGB are similar, which indicates that the thiamine molecules have strong bonding ability with the surface of copper and can be adsorbed tightly on the surface of copper.

text: Currently, there are few studies on the leveling efect of thiamine applied to electroplated copper deposition, and this study is the first study of the leveling efect of thiamine. Therefore, the energy gap value, Δ E, characterizes the adsorption capacity of organic molecules on metal surfaces. The lower the Δ E, the stronger the adsorption capacity.

text: In this experiment, through theoretical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations, the diference between thiamine and the leveling agent JGB was compared, and it was determined that the adsorption capacity and adsorption behavior of thiamine on the copper surface would inhibit the deposition of copper better.

section: Prediction and Efect Verification of Thiamine as a Leveling Agent in Chip Wafer Electroplating > 4. CONCLUSIONS
text: In this experiment, through theoretical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations, the diference between thiamine and the leveling agent JGB was compared, and it was determined that the adsorption capacity and adsorption behavior of thiamine on the copper surface would inhibit the deposition of copper better. By conducting CV and CP tests on leveling agent JGB and new leveling agent thiamine, the study shows that the CV oxidation peak area obtained after adding thiamine is smaller than that of adding JGB, and the potential diference of thiamine at high and low rotational speeds \triangle η=87~ mV > 5 0 ~ mV, suggesting its potential as a leveling agent.

section: Prediction and Efect Verification of Thiamine as a Leveling Agent in Chip Wafer Electroplating > 4. CONCLUSIONS
text: By conducting CV and CP tests on leveling agent JGB and new leveling agent thiamine, the study shows that the CV oxidation peak area obtained after adding thiamine is smaller than that of adding JGB, and the potential diference of thiamine at high and low rotational speeds \triangle η=87~ mV > 5 0 ~ mV, suggesting its potential as a leveling agent. Through EIS testing, it was found that the addition of thiamine not only inhibited the Cu ^2 + → Cu ^+ reaction but also suppressed the Cu ^+ → Cu reaction.

section: Prediction and Efect Verification of Thiamine as a Leveling Agent in Chip Wafer Electroplating > 4. CONCLUSIONS
text: Through EIS testing, it was found that the addition of thiamine not only inhibited the Cu ^2 + → Cu ^+ reaction but also suppressed the Cu ^+ → Cu reaction. Through electroplating experiments, it was found that thiamine has a leveling efect on copper deposition and can be applied to wafer microhole electroplating. Moreover, in wafer electroplating, it was found that without adding inhibitors, only 55 mg/L Cl −, 6 mg/L SPS, and 4 mg/L thiamine as leveling agents can achieve a good filling efect.
